newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schneider charged with fraud in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Schneider charged with fraud in Germany.

text.p: The Frankfurt prosecutor's office said Monday it filed fraud charges against former property tycoon Juergen Schneider in connection with the collapse of his real estate empire in 1994.

The office said it had charged Schneider on Dec. 17 with credit fraud in two cases, serious fraud in three cases and with one case of bankruptcy. The charges carry a maximum sentence of 15 years in prison.

Schneider, once one of Germany's most celebrated entrepreneurs, fell from grace when he and his wife vanished in April 1994, leaving their company to crumble under more than 5 billion marks ($3.2 billion) of debt.
The Schneiders were detained in Miami in 1995 after a year-long international manhunt. They returned voluntarily to Germany last February to face questioning. He is being held in a Frankfurt prison.

Prosecutors allege Schneider obtained credit from banks under false pretenses, by overstating his rental income and presenting forged bills. They also allege he contributed to the bankruptcy of his group by transferring 245 million marks ($158 million) to Switzerland.

Schneider's disappearance in April 1994 as his empire collapsed, and later the bankruptcy of his group, exposed his creditor banks to public outrage at the apparent ease with which he obtained funding from them.
